questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question tests the ability to derive and implement online statistics for real-time trend detection, emphasizing constant-time per-sample updates and memory efficiency.

## Key Concepts
- **Online (one-pass) statistics**: Computing regression without storing individual data points
- **Running sums**: Maintaining sufficient statistics for linear regression
- **Time-space trade-off**: O(1) updates vs O(n) reprocessing

## Per-Element Update
Each new sample (t, v_t) requires:
```javascript
n     += 1;
sumX += t;
sumY += v_t;
sumXX += t * t;
sumXY += t * v_t;
```

## Memory Usage
O(1) — only five scalar values are stored regardless of the number of samples processed.

## Concrete Example
Suppose sensor values arrive as v_1=3, v_2=5, v_3=7:

| t | v_t | n  | sumX | sumY | sumXX | sumXY |
|---|-----|----|------|------|-------|-------|
| 1 | 3   | 1  | 1    | 3    | 1     | 3     |
| 2 | 5   | 2  | 3    | 8    | 5     | 13    |
| 3 | 7   | 3  | 6    | 15   | 14    | 34    |

After t=3: m = (3·34 - 6·15) / (3·14 - 6²) = (102 - 90) / (42 - 36) = 12/6 = 2, matching the obvious trend v_t = 2t+1.

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design scalable approximate graph metrics under online updates; bridges sampling theory with dynamic algorithms.

## Key Concepts
- Landmark-based approximations
- Incremental shortest-path relaxations
- Trade-offs: accuracy ε vs. update cost δ

## Code Example
```javascript
// Pseudocode: initialize landmarks, compute dist from each landmark
for each l in landmarks:
  dist[l] = Dijkstra(l, G)
// On batch update
for edge in batch:
  updateGraph(edge)
  for l in landmarks:
    relaxPathsFrom(l, affectedSubgraph)
// Top-k query uses aggregated scores
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How to adapt s and δ in response to observed error? 
- How do deletions or edge weight changes affect guarantees and cost?
